_readme: THE CONTENT RATING (IARC) QUESTIONNAIRE ANSWERS — Subly, channel `android-play`.
🔴 THIS FILE RECORDS ANSWERS. IT DOES NOT RECORD A RATING, AND IT MUST NOT.
Google is explicit that the developer does not decide the rating: 'Your app's content ratings are
assigned by separate rating authorities and determined by your questionnaire responses', and 'each
rating authority uses its own methodology to assign ratings' (see `sources`). A rating written into
this file before the questionnaire has been submitted would be a number nobody computed, sitting in
the repository looking authoritative — the exact failure this codebase has already deleted an
invented store limit for. `assignedRating` is therefore null, `status` says why, and
tooling/ci/assert-play-declarations.mjs FAILS if a rating string appears without an IARC certificate
and its citation beside it.
⚠️ THE EXACT CONSOLE WORDING OF EACH QUESTION IS UNVERIFIED — see `questionnaireWording`. The IARC
questionnaire is only rendered inside the Play Console after it is started; it is not on a public
page and it was not fetched. So this file records SUBSTANTIVE CLAIMS ABOUT THE APP'S CONTENT, each
with the basis for it, rather than pretending to mirror a form nobody here has read. When the
questionnaire is actually opened, each console question maps onto one or more claims below, and any
question that maps onto none is a gap this file has to grow a row for.
Google: 'Make sure to provide accurate responses to the content rating questionnaire' and
'Misrepresentation of your app's content may result in its removal or suspension.' Every claim below
is therefore either DERIVED from the tree — with `tells` a guard checks — or marked `humanOwned`
with the reason it cannot be derived. There is no third category, and a claim with neither is a
build failure.
⚠️ NOT LEGAL ADVICE AND NOT WRITTEN BY A LAWYER, the same disclaimer tooling/legal/README.md carries.
statusReason: The questionnaire has not been submitted. The Play organisation account was verified 2026-08-04 and the questionnaire is a per-app, one-time Console action. Until it is submitted there is no rating, no IARC certificate, and nothing here that could honestly be filled in — which is the state this file is designed to represent rather than paper over.

ratingIsAssignedNotChosen.quote: Your app's content ratings are assigned by separate rating authorities and determined by your questionnaire responses; each rating authority uses its own methodology to assign ratings.

accuracyRule.quote: Make sure to provide accurate responses to the content rating questionnaire. Misrepresentation of your app's content may result in its removal or suspension.

authorities._why: Recorded because one questionnaire yields SEVERAL ratings, one per authority, and a later 'what rating did we get' question has more than one answer. Listed from the same fetch as `sources.ratingIsAssignedNotChosen`.

questionnaireWording.why: The IARC questionnaire is rendered inside the Play Console after the developer starts it and is not published on any page that could be fetched and cited. No verbatim question text is reproduced here, because inventing plausible question wording would make this file look like a filled-in form while being a guess about someone else's UI.
questionnaireWording.consequence: The claims below are about the APP, not about the form. Mapping them onto the console's actual questions is a human step, and `humanOwned.mapClaimsToConsoleQuestions` records it as one.

claims.claim: Subly is an application, not a game. The questionnaire branches on this at the first question and the whole downstream question set differs.
claims.basis: The listing category this repository submits is the one in category.txt, checked here for equality — so a change to a game category makes this claim fail rather than leaving a questionnaire answered as 'app' for a listing filed under Games.

claims.claim: The app offers digital purchases: its own premium subscription, presented in-app, with purchase execution OFF-DEVICE on the apex web checkout ([ADR 038]).
claims.basis: FLIPPED 2026-08-08 with productization P2.4b — the same commit that made nikatru_purchases a direct dependency; this claim's tells named that package in advance precisely so the dep and the answer could never move separately. What is offered: the app's own subscription tiers (offerings read from the platform catalog; purchase surface = PaywallGate → the apex web page nikatru.com/pricing?app=subly, [ADR 038]) — still no Play Billing and no on-device payment instrument (data-safety.json's Purchase-history clientAbsence carries that claim). At the time of the flip the rail has ZERO call sites (the first money surface lands with P2.6a; the paywall flip is Phase 4), so this answer leads the code — which is how a rating questionnaire is filled: it describes the product Play RATES at submission (A-3, owner-gated, post-Phase-4). If the store lane is ever decided to ship free-only permanently, flip this back WITH that decision. The tells stay as written — the guard tolerates a tell absent while the answer is true, and the set now enforces that this answer can never quietly return to false while a money-path package remains. (The old basis's 'packages/purchases is deliberately not a dependency' and its tombstone citation pubspec.yaml:92-97 — now :123-131 — expired with [ADR 036]/[ADR 037].)

claims.claim: The app contains no advertising of any kind, and no advertising or attribution SDK.

formatCrossCheck.why: 🔴 THE TELLS BELOW CANNOT SEE A HOUSE AD, AND THIS ANSWER WOULD STAY GREEN WHILE BECOMING FALSE. Every tell here is a package or a permission; Google's own ads triggers include one that needs neither — 'House ads: My app renders a small ad banner, interstitial ad, ad wall, and/or widget'. A promotional surface is UI we render, so it adds no dependency and nothing in `dependency-tells` moves. The format-keyed derivation lives in the file named above and the guard compares the two answers on every run: they are the same sentence sworn to two authorities and they may not disagree. Added 2026-08-09 (research/44 §3 V3, defect 2).

claims.basis: No ads SDK, no attribution SDK, no advertising-ID permission. The app's own analytics code states the rule positively — analytics_providers.dart:56, 'Never a device ad-ID' — and the consent prompt tells the user 'No name, no email, no advertising ID and no IP address.' The tells make it a build failure rather than a promise. ⚠️ THE TELLS ARE NOT THE WHOLE ANSWER: they are package-keyed, and the Play question is format-keyed. See `formatCrossCheck` — that half is derived from the widget tree and the served config, and it is what a house ad would trip.

claims.claim: The app contains no gambling, simulated gambling, loot boxes, or real-money wagering.
claims.basis: There is no chance mechanic and no wagering surface anywhere in the app; the screens are a subscription list, a calendar grid of renewal dates, a budget figure and settings. THE TELL SET NARROWED IN P2.4b (2026-08-08): nikatru_purchases left it when it became a direct dependency, because its presence no longer proves what the old set's logic rested on — 'no money path at all ⇒ nothing can be staked'. What replaces that proof: the first-party rail is single-purpose by construction — fixed-price offerings for the app's OWN subscription, read from the platform catalog, with checkout on the apex web page ([ADR 038]) — no arbitrary-payment surface a wager could ride on and no chance mechanic reachable through a fixed-price subscription. The four remaining package tells and the BILLING permission stay armed: any of THOSE appearing means someone added a generic on-device payment path, and this claim must be re-derived, not re-worded.

claims.claim: Users cannot interact with, message, or exchange content with other users. There is no social surface.
claims.basis: Subly is single-user by construction. Every data route on services/subly-api is scoped to the caller's own user_id — there is no route that returns another user's rows, no profile surface, no comment, share or invite. The dependency tells cover the mechanism by which a chat or realtime surface would arrive. ⚠️ PARTIALLY HUMAN-OWNED: 'no route reads another user's rows' is a property of the route handlers that this guard does not re-derive; it is asserted by services/subly-api's own tests and by assert-platform-register.mjs, and a reviewer adding a shared surface must update this claim. Recorded in `humanOwned.noSharedSurface`.

claims.claim: The app does not share a user's physical location with other users.
claims.basis: Vacuously true twice over: the app never obtains a location (no permission, no package — the same tells as data-safety.json's Location rows) and has no user-to-user surface to share one on (see `user-to-user-interaction`).

claims.claim: The app does not share personal information with third parties.

crossCheck.why: 🔴 THE ONE PLACE THESE TWO FORMS CAN CONTRADICT EACH OTHER, AND THE CONTRADICTION IS INVISIBLE BECAUSE THEY ARE FILLED IN ON DIFFERENT SCREENS MONTHS APART. If any Data safety answer is ever set to shared:true and this stays false, one of the two declarations to Google is false — and Play checks both. So this answer is not written independently; it is DERIVED from the Data safety answers and fails the moment they disagree.

claims.basis: Every data type in data-safety.json declares shared:false in both postures. The infrastructure that receives data — Cloudflare, Supabase, the self-hosted GlitchTip on Oracle Cloud — is service-provider processing on our behalf, which Play's own definition of 'shared' excludes.

claims.claim: Subly is not designed for or targeted at children.

crossCheck.why: The Data safety form's 'Committed to follow the Play Families Policy' badge and the content rating's target-audience answer are the same claim asked twice. Declaring the badge on one screen and 'not for children' on the other is a contradiction a human filling in two forms weeks apart will not catch.

claims.basis: A subscription-cost tracker with an account, a budget and no child-directed content. ⚠️ THE UNDERLYING JUDGEMENT IS A HUMAN'S — nothing in a repository can derive an intended audience — but the CONSISTENCY of the two declarations is mechanical, and that is what is enforced here.

claims.claim: The app contains no violence, sexual content, nudity, profanity, crude humour, horror, or references to drugs, alcohol or tobacco.
claims.basis: ⚠️ HUMAN-OWNED, AND SAID SO RATHER THAN FAKED. There is no mechanical tell for 'does this app contain violence'. A keyword scan over the listing copy and the app's strings would be an assertion that cannot fail on any realistic input — it would inflate apparent coverage while checking nothing, which this repository deletes on sight. What a guard CAN do is refuse to let this claim sit here without a named owner and a named set of surfaces to re-read; both are recorded, and `humanOwned.affirmContentDescriptors` is the item that closes it. The surfaces listed are the complete set a reviewer must look at: the listing copy, the screenshots and the app's own strings.

_why: The claims a repository genuinely cannot derive, named individually so they are visible on every run
instead of hiding inside a claim that looks checked. tooling/ci/assert-play-declarations.mjs PRINTS
each of these rather than failing the build — per the standing rule this codebase uses for owner-gated
gaps (assert-seams-wired.mjs, [pipeline C-6]): failing CI on work only a human can do blocks
everything else and teaches people to switch the guard off.
humanOwned.affirmContentDescriptors: A human must read apps/subly/store/android-play/long-description.txt, short-description.txt, the screenshots and the app's own strings, and affirm that none contains violence, sexual content, nudity, profanity, crude humour, horror, or drug/alcohol/tobacco references, before submitting the questionnaire. Re-affirmed whenever listing copy or screenshots change.
humanOwned.mapClaimsToConsoleQuestions: The IARC questionnaire's exact questions are only visible inside the Play Console. When it is opened, each console question must be matched to one or more claims above; any console question matching none of them means this file is missing a row and must grow one before the questionnaire is submitted.
humanOwned.noSharedSurface: The `user-to-user-interaction` claim rests partly on 'no route on services/subly-api returns another user's rows'. That is true of every handler today and is asserted by that Worker's own tests, but this guard does not re-derive it. Anyone adding a shared or social surface must update the claim in the same change.
humanOwned.recordTheOutcome: When the questionnaire is submitted, the resulting IARC certificate id and the per-authority ratings go into `assignedRating` and `iarcCertificate` WITH a source. Until then both stay null and the guard enforces it.
